eventMetadata.context_description: Latest ensemble forecasts from the Met Office and ECMWF place London’s maximum temperature on 16 August near 25–27 °C, with 26 °C emerging as the mode because model runs show modest afternoon cloud build-up and light south-westerly flow that caps peak values. Recent high-pressure dominance has produced above-climatology warmth, yet increasing mid-level moisture and a subtle trough approaching from the west introduce 1–2 °C of spread across members. Official guidance currently lists 27 °C, but surface observations and boundary-layer schemes differ on how quickly temperatures respond once insolation declines after 15:00 UTC. Updated model cycles and the morning Met Office forecast are the next data points likely to shift the tightly bunched 25–26 °C market probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from Météo-France and ECMWF models indicate a post-heatwave cooldown for Paris on August 16, with peak temperatures likely near 29°C under increasing cloud cover, light winds, and possible early showers that limit solar heating. Updated model outputs over the next 12–18 hours will clarify whether convective activity or clearer conditions push readings higher.

Traders’ near-even split between 35 °C and 34 °C mirrors this tight forecast range, with resolution hinging on the final official observation at Retiro or Barajas.
